Phase P.title: Parallel tracks — start on day one
Phase P.intro: Long lead times. Nothing here is code, and all of it blocks something later.

Phase 0.title: Repository foundations
Phase 0.intro: Blocks literally everything. Nothing else starts until this is green.

Phase 1.title: Domain contracts
Phase 1.intro: Defined before any implementation reads them. This is what makes three products buildable in parallel.

Phase 2.title: Platform primitives
Phase 2.intro: No UI. These are the things every later layer depends on and that fail quietly if rushed.

Phase 3.title: Render engine core
Phase 3.intro: Headless. The engine must be complete and testable before anything draws a pixel of UI.

Phase 4.title: Pixel gate
Phase 4.intro: The instrument. Built before anything that could change pixels, so there is a baseline to compare against.

Phase 5.title: Transport — local
Phase 5.intro: Location-transparent from the first line. Local is an optimisation, not a different code path.

Phase 6.title: Playout service
Phase 6.intro: Headless and fully testable before its UI exists.

Phase 7.title: Editor service
Phase 7.intro: Also headless. Import, validation and publish must work before a designer sees a window.

Phase 8.title: MCP automation surface
Phase 8.intro: Deliberately before the UI. The application becomes fully operable and automatable while still headless.

Phase 9.title: UI research
Phase 9.intro: **Validation, not a gate (user decision Q1, 16 October 2026).** Phase 11 proceeded on the After Effects and XPression/Viz references (11.63, 15 October direction); these steps check that work with designers and operators. No Phase 11 step needs a Phase 9 step. The card sort (old 9.4) and three-direction concept test (old 9.6) were dropped.

Phase 10.title: Design system implementation
Phase 10.intro: Backend first — ingest and enforcement land before the panels that surface them.

Phase 11.title: Editor UI
Phase 11.intro: Deferred to here on purpose. Everything above is usable without it, and this is built against research output, not guesswork.

Phase 12.title: Playout UI
Phase 12.intro: Second because the control surface is smaller and the service beneath it is already proven. XPression/Viz conventions govern this surface; After Effects conventions govern the Editor. **First-release scope (user decision Q8, 16 October 2026):** sports/esports first. In scope: overlay layers with channel/layer targeting on one Program channel (12.10) and an as-run record (12.11). **Named out of scope, no rows yet:** MOS/NRCS newsroom integration, mirrored-engine failover, multiple output channels, programmable control panels, XPN/AMCP protocol adapters, switcher automation, GPI/GPO and tally.

Phase 13.title: Parity — the engine renders the viewport
Phase 13.intro: The gap-register item. Only possible once both the engine and the overlay architecture exist.

Phase 14.title: Remote engine
Phase 14.intro: Deployment change, not an architecture change — if the earlier phases held the line.

Phase 15.title: Output server and genlock
Phase 15.intro: External gate. Cannot be closed by engineering. Started at day one via P.1.

Phase 16.title: Content depth
Phase 16.intro: Feature work that is not release-blocking. Sequenced after parity and reliability.

Phase 17.title: Gen-AI template factory
Phase 17.intro: Depends only on Phases 1–8 plus the design system. Independent of the certification gates, so it moves at its own pace.

Phase 18.title: Figma import at full fidelity
Phase 18.intro: **Status: Planned (added 25 September 2026 at the user's request).** Figma is the primary design source. "Perfect" is not a feeling; it is defined here as two measurable things on a real corpus: **(a)** the imported scene renders within the pixel-gate threshold of Figma's own render of the same frame, and **(b)** the 7.2 compatibility report names every substitution, with zero unnamed ones. Anything Figma can express that the engine cannot is refused or substituted **by name**, never approximated silently (invariant 18). No Figma desktop or plugin host is required. The source is read through the Figma REST API and retained beside the template (7.2 "source retained"). Every imported layer stays an ordinary scene object, so every layer is animatable.

Phase 19.title: GrapiX Data Server (a DataLinq-class standalone application)
Phase 19.intro: **Status: Planned (added 25 September 2026 at the user's request).** This resolves the scoping decision deferred in the Phase 11 additions. Live data lives in its own **standalone application**, like Ross XPression DataLinq Server. It holds many data sources at once and serves them to both the Editor and Playout. Because it is a new process in the distributed architecture, its boundaries are fixed by an ADR before any code (19.1). Two constraints are carried in from existing invariants and must not be relaxed by that ADR: - the engine never fetches data itself, and a take stays intent-based; - the data a frame was rendered with is recorded with the take, so a frame can be reproduced.

rows.work: Project working colour space: compositing follows the project's declared colour space
rows.done_when: `WorkingColorSpace` offers sRGB (display-referred) and linear sRGB, with no default. A project declares one — new projects sRGB; a project created before 3.15, with no declaration, reads as linear sRGB, the space it was authored in — and an unreadable declaration refuses by name. Every scene carries its project's space (scene schema 3; a schema 1 or 2 scene upgrades losslessly to linear sRGB, proven against a witness saved by the schema-2 build), and reading or writing a scene whose space differs from its project's refuses by name. The engine converts tagged sources into the scene's space once, composites there, and applies the sRGB Preview or Rec.709/BT.1886 Program transform once: a rendered 50% black-over-white overlap gives each space's independently computed reference value to ±1 code value at both outputs, and the reference operations for anti-aliased coverage, gradient interpolation and blur averaging, which 3.16, 3.17 and 3.22 must match, are tested in both spaces. The pixel-gate baselines and the colour ramp are unchanged; ADR-0002 B.1 and the contract docs state the rule

rows.work: Multi-scene workspace: scenes as first-class entities
rows.done_when: A broadcast carries many graphics, so each open scene is a distinct session owning its own document, selection, playhead, collapse state and undo history; one workspace module lists every open scene and switches the active one; viewport, object manager, inspector, timeline, animation and binding panels are children of the active scene and render it alone; switching preserves each scene's own state, an edit or undo in one scene cannot alter another, and closing a scene with unsaved changes refuses by name

rows.work: Save model: Ctrl+S saves in place, Ctrl+Shift+S saves a new version
rows.done_when: Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) writes the active scene to its own file or project entry in place, and a saved preset into the project's preset library in place; it never creates a version. Ctrl+Shift+S (Cmd+Shift+S) is the only way to create a new version: the next free numbered copy (`<name>_v002`, `_v003`, …) is written beside the current one, the previous version is left byte-identical, and the session continues in the new version. Neither shortcut fires while a text field has focus; a failed save keeps the unsaved mark and names its reason

rows.work: One command registry behind every menu, toolbar, shortcut and agent action

rows.work: Menu bar and toolbar (After Effects conventions)
rows.done_when: A classic in-app menu bar — **File**: New Project, Open Project, Open Recent, Save (Ctrl+S), Save New Version (Ctrl+Shift+S), Save As…, Export package (7.6), Close Scene, Exit; **Edit**: Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete (Delete key), Select All; **Composition**; **Layer**; **View**; **Window**; **Help** — plus a slim toolbar of the common commands, identical on Windows and macOS. rows.done_when: Re-importing the same file updates the existing scenes in place, keyed by the Figma node id. Animation channels, phases, bindings and control fields on unchanged nodes are preserved. A deleted node that still carried animation or bindings is reported by name, not dropped silently

rows.work: Import UI for Figma
rows.done_when: Paste a Figma file or frame link, pick frames from thumbnails, see the coverage and substitution report before confirming, and land in one scene tab per frame

rows.work: ADR-0004: Data Server boundaries
rows.done_when: Accepted ADR fixing: process model (desktop app plus headless service mode), transport (reuses the 5.x control plane and gx1 tokens, 2.9), who resolves a binding at take time (Playout, never the engine), how values reach the engine (as data carried with the take intent), revision pinning of data, and failure policy per field (refuse, hold last good, or warn)

rows.work: Data contract
rows.done_when: `DataSource`, `DataTable`, `DataRecord` and typed `DataField` values, plus a source revision and timestamp and a staleness state, defined in Rust (`gx-contracts`) with TS generated; round-trips both ways; a schema change is a named event, never silent

rows.work: Standalone Data Server app
rows.done_when: Its own Tauri 2 executable, installable separately from Editor and Playout. It lists sources, their status, last update, error and sample rows, and also runs headless as a service on a playout machine

rows.work: Connectors: files and web
rows.done_when: CSV, Excel (xlsx), JSON and XML from a file, HTTP (with a poll interval) or WebSocket, RSS/Atom, and manually edited tables. Each connector detects schema drift and names it, and a file watch uses 2.5

rows.work: Connectors: databases and sheets
rows.done_when: SQL through PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and ODBC; Google Sheets. Source credentials live in the OS keychain and never appear in scenes, packages, logs or the MCP surface

rows.work: Many sources, change propagation and staleness
rows.done_when: Multiple sources run concurrently. Subscribers get a snapshot then ordered deltas. The last good value is retained, and staleness past a source's declared limit is surfaced to every subscriber (never silently stale). A deliberately stalled fixture feed produces its declared 19.1 state (hold last good or refuse the update), never a guessed value. Reconnect resumes from a revision without a full reload

rows.work: Editor reads the Data Server
rows.done_when: The Data binding panel browses sources, tables and fields from a running server; binding a property to a server field writes a portable reference, not the value; sample data for preview is a pinned snapshot, so a scene previews offline

rows.work: Playout reads the Data Server
rows.done_when: At cue/take, Playout resolves each bound field from the server and sends the values with the intent. The committed frame records the data revision it used. A missing or stale field follows the 19.1 policy and names the field; a feed value whose type does not match the bound field is refused by name. Output is never blocked on a slow source without saying so

rows.work: Data Server soak and failure tests
rows.done_when: Eight hours with at least 20 sources at mixed update rates, source outages, server restarts and network loss; zero silent staleness and zero takes rendered with unrecorded data

rows.work: Live esports data and an AI suggestion lane
rows.done_when: Esports feeds (GRID or others) ingest into a typed, timestamped model with deterministic triggers; data reaches the engine only as Control-plane intent. Suggestions need producer confirmation unless their class is pre-approved. Replaying a recorded feed produces the same trigger sequence on every run; a suggestion never changes Program without a confirm action or a pre-approved class
